evidence: DESIGN-NOTES.md:39 states the intended named composed hydration can have its seats and threads listed, retired, and resurrected together, while acknowledging its exact lifecycle is open. Reproduce: hydrate a named feature group with seats A/B and thread X; later add seat C for that feature, retire B locally, or switch to a copied template with corresponding member IDs (DESIGN-NOTES.md:74-75,293-296; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:23-26). On a later 'list/retire/resurrect this group' request, the grouped hydration action records only the seats created/reused by that action for undo (DESIGN-NOTES.md:285-286,300-302); independent seat IDs and member correspondence do not specify whether C or retired B is a current member, or whether the later template state changes membership. Applying only the original action set omits C; applying current template members may recreate/exclude B or misclassify reused seats. Thus the collective operation cannot be determined from the stated contract, contrary to the named-group experience in line 39. This is an acknowledged open design contract; it does not require an extra runtime group node, only defined membership semantics. No external premise is needed.
